BiblicalUsage: This word for the mighty is used only of God — never of men. Jacob blesses Joseph by the hands of ‘the mighty God of Jacob’; David vows to the mighty God of Jacob and will not rest until he finds Him a dwelling; and Isaiah calls the LORD ‘the mighty One of Israel’ who will ease Himself of His adversaries.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word is set apart on purpose: might belongs to God in a way it belongs to no man. The same Scriptures that call Him the Mighty One show kings boasting in their own strength and falling, and I would rather rest in His might than trust my own.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
